title: Families of California murder victims ask state Supreme Court to block governor’s commutation of death sentences | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

More than two dozen family members of murder victims in California are asking the state Supreme Court to blockGov. Gavin Newsom’s decisionto commute the sentences of everyone on the state’s Death Row.

“Thousands of jurors and hundreds of judges set aside their personal views on the merits of the death penalty to render judgments based on the evidence and the law,” statesthe petition, which was filed Monday. “Governor Newsom decided his personal views should override all those who actually participated in the process, followed and applied the law.”

The petitioners include Marc Klaas, whose 12-year-old daughter Polly was abducted and murdered in 1993. After Newsom’s commutation announcement on November 5, Klaastold CNN, “The criminal justice system can turn on a whim.”

Newsom’s announcement was applauded by death penalty opponents, includingthe ACLUandPaul Wilson, thehusband of a murder victim, who initially supported the execution of his wife’s killer before changing his mind about the death penalty.

The murdered victims’ families who filed the petition, along with a coalition of prosecutors and crime victims’ advocates, say that although Newsom has met with some victims’ families in the past, the governor failed to provide the required legal notice to victims before announcing his decision.

In an open letter announcing his decision, Newsom called the state’s system for administering the death penalty “a failure.”

“Many Californian feel that those who commit brutal crimes deserve to die,” Newsomwrote. “But as Governor, I have concluded the state cannot morally kill them.”

Under the California Constitution, the Supreme Court must affirm any commutation recommended by the governor for a felon who has more than one felony conviction, a condition met by about 70% of all condemned inmates in California, theHabeas Corpus Resource Centersays.

California’s capital cases have long been legally and procedurally stalled, with Newsom putting a formal moratorium on executions in place in 2019. California has not carried out a death sentence in 20 years and has the most populous Death Row in the United States, according to theDeath Penalty Information Center.

CNN’s Dahlia Faheid and Elizabeth Wolfe contributed to this report.
